instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle.
Peel the garlic. Mince 5 cloves and smash the other 6 with the flat of a knife. Slice the potatoes into 1/4 inch rounds and cut the onion into 8 wedges.
In a large roasting pan, toss the potatoes, onion and smashed garlic with 3 tbsp of the oil and 1 tsp of the salt. Spread them in a single layer.
Pat the chicken dry. Rub it with 1 tbsp of the oil, 1 tsp salt, the black pepper, the seven spice and the cumin.
Lay the thighs skin side up on top of the vegetables.
In a bowl, whisk the minced garlic, the remaining 2 tbsp oil, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt, the broth and the juice of 1 lemon plus half of the second. That should be about 1/4 cup of juice.
Pour the sauce around the chicken so the skin stays dry. Slice the remaining half lemon into rounds and tuck them in among the potatoes.

Bake for 45 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the chicken is golden. You're cooking the thighs to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece near the bone. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when the juices run clear.
Switch the oven to broil. Cook for 5 to 8 minutes, until the skin is deep golden. Watch it closely so it doesn't burn.
Let it rest for 5 minutes. Chop 1/4 cup of the parsley leaves and scatter them over the pan.
Taste the potatoes and the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or squeeze a lemon slice over it.
Serve with the lemon slices and the pan juices.
method_notes: The sources agree on bone-in chicken baked over potatoes in a lemon and garlic sauce. The Salt and Sweet version (5.0 stars from 68 visible ratings) is the lead, with raw potatoes, onion and a raw lemon garlic oil sauce. I took the seven spice and cumin from Mediterranean Living and Simply Lebanese, and a little broth from Simply Lebanese so the potatoes cook through without frying them first. I used thighs instead of drumsticks and baked at 400°F instead of 350°F to brown the skin.
